pr_comments: Marked this semver-major out of caution. If there are no surprises in CITGM I'm also ok with semver-patch as per https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/39400#issuecomment-890331101.
I noticed `aix` fails - it does so on other PRs as well.

I think this might be breaking a few ecosystem modules. Specifically:

* `undici`
* `pump`
* `hapi`
* `socket.io`

Those needs to be investigated.

Here is a CITGM (master) to see the status there for comparison: https://ci.nodejs.org/view/Node.js-citgm/job/citgm-smoker/2738/

> `pump` is already built into [Node.js](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/e579acb8dc4854a41442cac9ddb0221d7a44dbce/lib/internal/streams/pipeline.js).

It's still a module with a massive amount of downloads that we cannot break.
The error with `pump` also happens on the `master` run.

issue_context.title: http2: `end` is emitted before `error` when destroying client stream
comments: It's not possible as it's not possible to be connected in the same tick you initiate a connection.

> `pipeline` see the stream as correctly ended, that's why it swallows the error - its behavior is correct.

It's a duplex that emitted only `'end'`, it is still writable and the error is emitted before `'close'`. Is it the expected behavior for pipeline? Shouldn't it wait for `'error'` or `'close'` for a duplex?

Edit: I guess pipeline does not care about the writable side which makes sense as there is no more data to read/pipe to the next stream.
@mcollina In the issue the writable side has ended but the readable not.

> Edit: I guess pipeline does not care about the writable side which makes sense as there is no more data to read/pipe to the next stream.

@szmarczak from @lpinca words ^.
Looks like https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/89adc16ff0a66b447df3e12f82aa43e495665636/lib/internal/streams/readable.js#L1336 should be `state.errored` instead of `state.errorEmitted`
@mcollina I believe in that case `end` should be never emitted. https://nodejs.org/api/stream.html#stream_event_end_1

[http2 failed tests.txt](https://github.com/nodejs/node/files/6910232/http2.failed.tests.txt) with `state.errored` instead of `state.errorEmitted`. All the tests depend on the `end` event. If they used `close` instead, I think they would pass.
I would go with a patch as it's a bad bug. I'd just wait to backport to LTS lines for a bit (or at all).

> Looks like https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/89adc16ff0a66b447df3e12f82aa43e495665636/lib/internal/streams/readable.js#L1336 should be `state.errored` instead of `state.errorEmitted`

I _think_ so.

review_comments: Any reason for using `once()`? Wasn't `req.on('end', common.mustCall());` sufficient?

> Wasn't req.on('end', common.mustCall()); sufficient?

No in case of an error.
Doesn't this invalidate that specific condition? I mean it now throws also for `err.code === 'ECONNRESET'`. If that is wanted, why keeping the check in place?
Because we want either `end` or `error` :) If `end` is received then this check passes, if `error` gets emitted then the promise rejects and there's an empty catch - so no error is thrown outside.

~~Ah ok, I understand. Wouldn't it be more readable/easier to understand to remove  the `common.mustCall()` listener (`req.on('end', common.mustCall())`) and replace it with `common.mustNotCall()` from the listener of the `'error'` event?~~
Nevermind, the function returned by `common.mustCall()` must be called :).
Ah ok `stream.on('error', common.expectsError(expected));` was hidden in the diff.
